title: 串、并联谐振组成的选频电路
statement: 图示电路用来从信号中滤掉 ω = 1000 rad/s 的干扰、让 ω = 500 rad/s 的有用信号无衰减地送到负载 R = 50 Ω。L = 0.1 H，C₂ = 10 µF，C₁ = 30 µF。
(1) 求电路的最低谐振频率 f₀（从电源看进去阻抗为纯电阻）；(2) 设电源为 ω = 1000 rad/s 的干扰 U_s = 10∠0° V（有效值），求 L∥C₂ 两端电压 U_ab 和电感电流 I_L 的有效值；(3) 说明电路为什么能实现上述要求。

questions.explain: Z = R + 1/(jωC₁) + jωL/(1 − ω²LC₂)。虚部为零：1/(ωC₁) = ωL/(1 − ω²LC₂) → ω² = 1/(L(C₁ + C₂)) = 1/(0.1 × 40×10⁻⁶) = 2.5×10⁵，ω = 500 rad/s，f₀ ≈ 79.58 Hz（串联谐振）。

questions.ask: (2) ω = 1000 rad/s 时 U_ab 的有效值 = ?
questions.explain: 1/√(LC₂) = 1000 rad/s：L 与 C₂ 发生并联谐振，阻抗无穷大，支路电流为零。C₁ 和 R 上都没有电压，U_ab = U_s = 10 V。

questions.ask: (2) ω = 1000 rad/s 时电感电流有效值 I_L = ?
questions.explain: I_L = U_ab/(jωL) = 10/(j100) = −j0.1 A，有效值 0.1 A；C₂ 中电流 j0.1 A，两者在 L、C₂ 之间环流，流向 R 的电流为零。

questions.ask: (3) ω = 1000 rad/s（干扰）时负载电压 U_R 的有效值 = ?
questions.explain: ω = 1000 rad/s 时 L∥C₂ 并联谐振，相当于开路，干扰完全被阻断（陷波），U_R = 0。

questions.ask: (3) 若电源换成 ω = 500 rad/s、同样 10 V 的有用信号，U_R 的有效值 = ?
questions.explain: ω = 500 rad/s 时 L∥C₂ 呈感性（等效电感 L/(1 − ω²LC₂) = 0.1/0.75 = 0.1333 H，感抗 66.67 Ω），正好与 C₁ 的容抗 1/(500 × 30×10⁻⁶) = 66.67 Ω 串联谐振，相当于短路，U_R = U_s = 10 V。

hints: 先单独看 L∥C₂：它在 ω = 1/√(LC₂) 时并联谐振（阻抗 ∞）；低于这个频率呈感性，高于呈容性。
低于并联谐振频率时，L∥C₂ 的等效电感可以和 C₁ 串联谐振；写出总阻抗虚部 = 0 的方程。
solution: **1. L∥C₂ 的阻抗。** Z_p = jωL·(1/jωC₂)/(jωL + 1/jωC₂) = jωL/(1 − ω²LC₂)。并联谐振频率 ω_p = 1/√(LC₂) = 1/√(10⁻⁶) = 1000 rad/s。
**2. 串联谐振。** 总阻抗 Z = R − j/(ωC₁) + jωL/(1 − ω²LC₂)。令虚部为零：1 − ω²LC₂ = ω²LC₁ → ω_s = 1/√(L(C₁ + C₂)) = **500 rad/s**，f₀ = 500/(2π) ≈ **79.58 Hz**。这是最低的谐振频率（ω_p = 1000 rad/s 时阻抗 → ∞，是另一个“纯电阻”点）。
**4. ω = 500 rad/s。** Z_p = j50/(1 − 0.25) = j66.67 Ω，C₁ 的阻抗 −j66.67 Ω，二者相消，Z = R，U_R = U_s：有用信号无衰减通过。
**结论：** 并联谐振用来“阻断”（陷波），串联谐振用来“导通”，组合起来实现选频。

en.title: A frequency-selective circuit using series and parallel resonance
statement: The circuit shown is meant to remove an interfering signal at ω = 1000 rad/s and pass a useful signal at ω = 500 rad/s to the load R = 50 Ω without attenuation. L = 0.1 H, C₂ = 10 µF, C₁ = 30 µF.

(1) Find the lowest resonant frequency f₀ (where the impedance seen by the source is purely resistive). (2) With the source being the interference at ω = 1000 rad/s, V_s = 10∠0° V (rms), find the rms voltage V_ab across L∥C₂ and the rms inductor current I_L. (3) Explain why the circuit does what is required.

questions.explain: Z = R + 1/(jωC₁) + jωL/(1 − ω²LC₂). Zero imaginary part: 1/(ωC₁) = ωL/(1 − ω²LC₂) → ω² = 1/(L(C₁ + C₂)) = 1/(0.1 × 40×10⁻⁶) = 2.5×10⁵, ω = 500 rad/s, f₀ ≈ 79.58 Hz (series resonance).

questions.ask: (2) rms value of V_ab at ω = 1000 rad/s = ?
questions.explain: 1/√(LC₂) = 1000 rad/s: L and C₂ are in parallel resonance, their impedance is infinite and the branch current is zero. There is no voltage across C₁ or R, so V_ab = V_s = 10 V.

questions.ask: (2) rms inductor current I_L at ω = 1000 rad/s = ?
questions.explain: I_L = V_ab/(jωL) = 10/(j100) = −j0.1 A, rms 0.1 A; C₂ carries j0.1 A. The current circulates between L and C₂, and none flows on to R.

questions.ask: (3) At ω = 1000 rad/s (the interference), rms load voltage V_R = ?
questions.explain: At ω = 1000 rad/s, L∥C₂ is in parallel resonance and acts as an open circuit: the interference is completely blocked (a notch), V_R = 0.

questions.ask: (3) If the source is instead the wanted 10 V signal at ω = 500 rad/s, rms V_R = ?
questions.explain: At ω = 500 rad/s, L∥C₂ is inductive (equivalent inductance L/(1 − ω²LC₂) = 0.1/0.75 = 0.1333 H, reactance 66.67 Ω) and forms a series resonance with C₁ (reactance 1/(500 × 30×10⁻⁶) = 66.67 Ω): a short, so V_R = V_s = 10 V.

hints: Look at L∥C₂ on its own first: it is in parallel resonance (infinite impedance) at ω = 1/√(LC₂); below that it is inductive, above it capacitive.
Below the parallel resonance, the equivalent inductance of L∥C₂ can be in series resonance with C₁; write the equation 'imaginary part of the total impedance = 0'.
solution: **1. Impedance of L∥C₂.** Z_p = jωL·(1/jωC₂)/(jωL + 1/jωC₂) = jωL/(1 − ω²LC₂). Parallel resonance at ω_p = 1/√(LC₂) = 1/√(10⁻⁶) = 1000 rad/s.

**2. Series resonance.** Total impedance Z = R − j/(ωC₁) + jωL/(1 − ω²LC₂). Zero imaginary part: 1 − ω²LC₂ = ω²LC₁ → ω_s = 1/√(L(C₁ + C₂)) = **500 rad/s**, f₀ = 500/(2π) ≈ **79.58 Hz**. This is the lowest resonance (at ω_p = 1000 rad/s the impedance → ∞, the other 'purely resistive' point).
**3. At ω = 1000 rad/s.** Z_p → ∞, the source current is I = 0, V_C₁ = 0 and V_R = 0, so V_ab = V_s = **10 V**; I_L = 10/(j100) = −j0.1 A, rms **0.1 A**, and I_C₂ = +j0.1 A.
**4. At ω = 500 rad/s.** Z_p = j50/(1 − 0.25) = j66.67 Ω, C₁'s impedance is −j66.67 Ω; they cancel, Z = R and V_R = V_s: the useful signal passes without attenuation.
**Conclusion:** parallel resonance 'blocks' (a notch) and series resonance 'passes'; combining them gives frequency selection.
